description: Hand-curated 10-fixture regression for the new inferential-structural-judge agent (AGENT-1) — the Inferential-FB sensor that closes the behaviour-harness gap Böckeler (2026-04, L465-478) punts on. The agent scores a session's diff against 4 fixed dimensions (over_engineering, arch_drift, test_pattern, doctrine_conformance) and journals a verdict with score 1-3=accept, 4-6=flag, 7-10=escalate per docs/research/inferential-structural-judge-design.md §3. These fixtures are the explicit countermeasure to the L476 test-quality problem ('we put a lot of faith into the AI-generated tests, that's not good enough yet'): 5 known-good diffs (expected score < 4, accept) and 5 known-bad diffs (expected score > 7, escalate), with hand-written rationales citing the design-doc section each fixture validates. Plan Q9: bucket pass criterion >= 4/5 in each bucket. Plan Q12 + design doc §4(c): the agent must NEVER emit permissionDecision; the autonomy invariant (ADR 0002 §L112) is the load-bearing guard, CI-enforced by `git grep -n 'permissionDecision' agents/inferential-structural-judge.md hooks/inferential-structural-judge-on-session-end.sh` returning 0 matches. Marked `manual` because the agent file (AGENT-1) and the eval-gate dispatcher (EVAL-1) are not yet integrated at FIX-1 ship time; the runner skips these with a note and EVAL-1 will lift the tag when it author the integration. The fixture is data only — EVAL-1 owns eval/run-eval.py and the bucket-threshold logic.

evals.task: Synthetic session in which a single file (skills/foo/scripts/bar.sh) was touched. The diff is exactly one line: a 1-character typo fix inside a method comment block (e.g. `# Recives input` -> `# Receives input`). No code, no logic, no test, no schema. `git diff --stat` shows 1 file, +1/-1. The session touched no other files. No prior verdict for this path exists in the journal (first-run state for the path). The agent should score this 1-2 (accept, silent) and top_finding should be 'no structural concerns' — a 1-line comment typo is the canonical no-op diff.
evals.rationale: Validates design doc §3 — the 1-3 score band is 'silent accept' and the agent must NOT invent a finding to justify a higher score (per the agent file's Voice section). Also validates the negative-space test: the agent does not over-flag trivial changes. If this fixture fails (agent scores >= 4), it has regressed to a paranoia posture and would bury the journal with noise on the kind of edits that make up ~40% of real session-end activity. Dimension targets: all four at 1 (clean across the board). Failure mode this guards: `inferential-judge-over-flags-trivial-diffs`.

evals.task: Synthetic session that adds a 3-line `bash -n` style syntax guard to an existing hook script in hooks/. The diff is small and surgical: `set -euo pipefail` is already present (so no new shell-strictness change), the guard appears immediately after the existing `source` block, and uses the same `hook_audit_log` helper from _lib.sh that every other hook in the repo uses. No new abstractions, no new top-level functions, no new env vars. `git diff --stat` shows 1 file, +3/-0.
evals.rationale: Validates design doc §3's `doctrine_conformance` and `test_pattern` dimensions. The guard is the *existing* pattern — `hook_audit_log` from `_lib.sh` is the canonical channel; using it is the *opposite* of test-pattern regression. The agent should score: test_pattern=2 (no test, no regression possible; the dimension defaults low), doctrine_conformance=1 (matches the existing 13-hook convention), over_engineering=1, arch_drift=1. If the agent scores >= 4 here, it has misread 'defensive programming' as 'over-engineering' — the exact failure mode Q9's '5 known-good' bucket exists to catch. Failure mode this guards: `inferential-judge-confuses-defensive-programming-with-over-engineering`.

evals.task: Synthetic session that adds a new agent file at agents/<new-name>.md. The file has frontmatter (name, description, tools allowlist) and the three canonical sections required by audit check #31.1: '## Input Contract', '## Output Format', '## Failure Modes'. The description is <= 1536 chars (the audit #31 cap). The `tools:` allowlist is `Read, Grep, Bash` with NO `disallowedTools:` block (the decay-cadence convention). The agent file is ~80 lines — focused, not sprawling. `git diff --stat` shows 1 file, +80/-0. No other files touched.
evals.rationale: Validates design doc §3's `doctrine_conformance` dimension on the happy path: a new agent that *follows* the 3-canonical-section pattern (audit #31.1) is the *correct* surface, not a doctrinal drift. The agent should score: doctrine_conformance=1 (matches the audit-required shape), arch_drift=1 (no responsibility moved, no BOUNDARY.md invariant broken — a new file at a registered plugin-surface path), over_engineering=1, test_pattern=1 (no test code in the diff). If the agent scores >= 4 here, it has lost the ability to distinguish 'new surface that follows the pattern' from 'new surface that invents a new pattern' — a critical regression because every new agent (including the judge's own AGENT-1 sibling) will trigger a false positive. Failure mode this guards: `inferential-judge-cannot-recognize-schema-compliant-new-surface`.

evals.task: Synthetic session that touches only CLAUDE.md (a single markdown file at the repo root). The diff is a prose-only edit: clarifying a section, fixing a typo in a code block, or updating a reference to a renamed file. No code, no test, no manifest, no schema, no plugin-surface. `git diff --stat` shows 1 file, +5/-3. No prior verdict for CLAUDE.md exists in the journal.
evals.rationale: Validates design doc §3's negative-space test on the doctrine_conformance dimension. A prose edit to a doctrine file is *itself* doctrine, but it is doctrine *conformance* — the diff matches the doc's stated purpose (clarifying, not contradicting). The agent should score: doctrine_conformance=1, arch_drift=1, over_engineering=1, test_pattern=1. If the agent scores >= 4 here, it has mis-applied doctrine_conformance as 'any change to a doctrine file is suspicious' — which would make every CLAUDE.md tweak a flag event and bury the journal. CLAUDE.md edits are a normal cadence event (decay-cadence quarterly sweep, ADR updates). Failure mode this guards: `inferential-judge-penalizes-doctrine-edits-as-suspect-by-default`.

evals.task: Synthetic session that fixes a small bug in skills/harness-audit/scripts/audit.sh. The fix is surgical: 1-2 lines changed, no new functions, no new flags, no new env vars, no change to the audit's external contract (same exit codes, same stdout shape, same stderr shape, same JSON envelope). The fix uses an existing helper from _lib.sh or extends an existing branch. `git diff --stat` shows 1 file, +2/-1. The audit's `## Output Format` section in its SKILL.md is unchanged. No tests added (the existing 38 sub-checks still cover the surface; the fix is a corner case the existing checks did not catch).
evals.rationale: Validates design doc §3's arch_drift and over_engineering dimensions on the surgical-fix happy path. A bug fix that does not change the audit's external contract is the *opposite* of architectural drift — it is architectural conformance. The agent should score: over_engineering=1 (no new primitive, no new layer), arch_drift=1 (no module responsibility moved; same exit codes, same envelope), doctrine_conformance=1, test_pattern=1. The 'no new test' concern is real but the test_pattern dimension targets *regressions* (tautologies, over-mocking) — adding no test is not the same as writing a bad test. If the agent scores >= 4 here, it has conflated 'no new test' with 'test pattern regression' and would penalize every small fix that the existing checks already cover. Failure mode this guards: `inferential-judge-conflates-missing-test-with-bad-test`.

evals.task: Synthetic session that adds a new wrapper class (e.g. `CacheLayer`, `SafeExecutor`, `RetryHelper`) around an existing single-call primitive that is already used directly by exactly one caller. The wrapper adds: (a) a config dataclass with 4 fields, (b) a factory function, (c) a context-manager entry/exit, (d) a `__repr__` for debug printing. The existing primitive is a module-private function in the same file. The new wrapper is 60+ lines. `git diff --stat` shows 1 file, +80/-0. No tests added (the wrapper has no failure mode the existing primitive did not already handle).
evals.rationale: Validates design doc §3's over_engineering dimension on the canonical anti-pattern: a new abstraction layer around a primitive with exactly one call site. The dimension's design-doc definition is 'is this diff solving a problem the harness does not have, or duplicating an existing primitive?' — this fixture is the textbook case for that question. The agent should score: over_engineering=4 (new layer with 4 surfaces, no new capability, single caller — the kind of topology inflation Böckeler L518 warns about), doctrine_conformance=1, arch_drift=2, test_pattern=2. If the agent scores < 7 here, it has lost the over_engineering dimension's discrimination power and the 2x2 Inferential FB cell has degraded to a posture-only check (the exact gap this whole plan exists to close). Failure mode this guards: `inferential-judge-blind-to-wrapper-layer-inflation`.

evals.task: Synthetic session that adds a `disallowedTools:` block to an existing agent file's frontmatter (e.g. `disallowedTools: [Edit, Write, NotebookEdit]`). The agent is a read-only review agent; the block is 'defensive' — meant to prevent the model from accidentally mutating files. `git diff --stat` shows 1 file, +3/-0. The agent's purpose is unchanged. The repo's decay-cadence convention explicitly forbids `disallowedTools:` (per .scratch/harness-decay-cadence.md, last_permission_review cadence row).
evals.rationale: Validates design doc §3's doctrine_conformance dimension on the decay-cadence anti-pattern. The dimension's design-doc definition names `disallowedTools:` as a hard rule violation: 'does the diff respect the doctrine's hard rules (no disallowedTools:, no model-driven mutation gates from inferential sensors, no plugin-cache-bypass, no permission drift)?' This fixture is the canonical case for that list. The agent should score: doctrine_conformance=5 (decay-cadence explicit anti-pattern, hits the dimension's highest bucket), over_engineering=2 (the change is small, but the *pattern* is the violation), arch_drift=1, test_pattern=1. If the agent scores < 7 here, it has lost the doctrine_conformance dimension's discrimination power on the very pattern the decay-cadence convention exists to prevent. The autonomy invariant (ADR 0002) is the symmetric guard: permission drift is *exactly* what `disallowedTools:` introduces. Failure mode this guards: `inferential-judge-misses-decay-cadence-disallowedtools-anti-pattern`.

evals.task: Synthetic session that adds a new matcher-less SessionEnd hook. The hook is a small LLM call (e.g. 'summarize what the session did') that, on detecting 'risky' content in the session summary, emits `permissionDecision: deny` on stdout via the PreToolUse JSON envelope. The hook is registered in hooks/hooks.json. The intent is 'a safety net' — block the next tool call if the session looked dangerous. The hook has no deterministic signal: the LLM call is the only check. `git diff --stat` shows 2 files (hooks/<new>.sh + hooks/hooks.json), +25/-0. No critical-hooks test added for the new gate.
evals.rationale: Validates design doc §4(c) — the autonomy invariant guard, the load-bearing anti-pattern. The design doc's verbatim language: 'It is the load-bearing guard against the L4-loop covert failure mode Böckeler's L356-359 warning points at: an inferential-FB sensor with permissionDecision: deny authority is a model-driven mutation gate, which the invariant forecloses. CI enforcement: `git grep -n 'permissionDecision' agents/inferential-structural-judge.md hooks/inferential-structural-judge-on-session-end.sh` must return zero matches.' This fixture is the *exact* pattern the invariant forecloses. The agent should score: doctrine_conformance=5 (autonomy invariant violation, the highest-severity doctrinal break), over_engineering=3 (model-driven mutation gate is its own over-engineering — solving a problem the existing computational-FF column already solves), arch_drift=2, test_pattern=1. If the agent scores < 9 here, the autonomy invariant has no operational guard and the L4-loop covert failure mode is live. This is the highest-severity bucket in the entire regression suite. Failure mode this guards: `inferential-judge-misses-autonomy-invariant-violation-permissiondecision-from-inferential-sensor`.

evals.task: Synthetic session that adds a forward database migration under scripts/migrations/. The migration drops a column from a table that exists in the schema (e.g. `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_settings;`). The migration file is a single .sql file with the forward statement only — no `*_reverse.sql` companion, no `BEGIN; ... COMMIT;` transaction wrapper, no `IF EXISTS` guard, no comment explaining the data-loss implication. `git diff --stat` shows 1 file, +5/-0. No doc update in docs/ explaining the migration. The harness's existing `scripts/run-acceptance.py` has a 5-exit-code contract (PASS/FAIL/INVOCATION/PARSE/BLOCK) and a reverse-migration check is part of the `BLOCK` exit code for irreversible operations.
evals.rationale: Validates design doc §3's arch_drift dimension on a data-loss-risk pattern. The dimension's design-doc definition is 'does this diff move a module's responsibility, or break a BOUNDARY.md invariant, in a way the existing patterns would not?' A migration that drops a column without a reverse-migration breaks a *data-integrity* invariant the existing pattern enforces (the run-acceptance.py BLOCK exit code, the doc-must-explain convention). The diff violates the pattern, not the data — the data is gone if anyone runs the forward migration on a real DB. The agent should score: arch_drift=4 (broken invariant, no companion reverse-migration file, no doc), doctrine_conformance=2 (the run-acceptance contract is doctrine, even if the harness is not yet using it for migrations — the dimension catches the gap), over_engineering=1, test_pattern=1. If the agent scores < 7 here, the arch_drift dimension has lost the discrimination power on data-integrity patterns, and the new harness surface (the inferential judge) is *less* protective than the existing run-acceptance contract. This is a regression-to-the-mean failure mode. Failure mode this guards: `inferential-judge-misses-data-loss-risk-migration-without-reverse`.
success_criteria: top_finding references reverse-migration or data-loss or BLOCK exit code
